Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
301 PM EDT Fri Sep 11 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Continue to monitor for a few thunderstorms in Central VA this
afternoon. Beyond that, the flood potential remains for Saturday
afternoon to evening, but uncertainty remains regarding where 
the heaviest rain will fall.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) A few Central Virginia thunderstorms today, then likely 
  widespread convection Saturday into Saturday night.

- 2) Dry conditions expected early next week ahead of a midweek
  cold front. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...

KEY MESSAGE 1...A few Central Virginia thunderstorms today, 
then likely widespread convection Saturday into Saturday night.

The slow moving frontal boundary is now across Central VA, with a 
few showers and thunderstorms noted along the I-64 corridor. SPC has 
a Marginal Risk (level 1 of 5) along the far southern CWA centered 
in Nelson County. This is where low-level convergence and better 
instability could result in a strong storm or two. The time window 
for impacts in our area are limited as the front continues to push 
south. Most of the convection pushes south of our area by around 4-
5PM. After that, conditions should be mostly dry through this 
evening. Cloud cover has kept temps in the 70s for most of the area, 
and even those north of the frontal boundary are also in the mid to 
upper 70s. 

Surface high pressure over southern New England slides offshore 
Saturday causing southeasterly flow to develop/strengthen over the 
Mid-Atlantic. The synoptic pattern gets messy into the weekend as an 
elongated trough stretches from the Deep South to Mid-Atlantic. The 
stalled boundary over southern VA lifts north as a warm front 
Saturday morning, bringing a possibly first round of showers to the 
area. As the boundary lifts north of the MD/PA border, warm sector 
showers are possible at time Saturday afternoon, though the bulk of 
convection is set to arrive toward the evening hours.

Numerous embedded shortwaves lift across the Tennessee Valley toward 
the southern Mid-Atlantic, helping produce ample lift and shear 
across the region. A surge of tropical moisture brings PWATs to 
around 2" Saturday afternoon into Saturday night. A wave of surface 
low pressure may try to develop somewhere in lee of the Alleghenies 
Saturday evening as the strongest shortwave traverses the region. A 
subtle jet streak develops ahead of the upper trough, and while not 
overly impressive it will be enough to aid in widespread showers and 
thunderstorm development. Locally heavy rain is likely in some 
areas, though the 12Z high res guidance does not point to any one 
specific location. Later analysis on areas of low-level convergence 
that set up will be key to determine where a flash flood threat 
could develop. But for now, have not issued any Flood Watches due to 
uncertainty in location of heaviest rain. WPC has expanded the 
Slight Risk area for excessive rainfall to include the Alleghenies 
where soils are more saturated from rain over the past month. Will 
continue to monitor the situation as new mesoscale guidance arrives.

A cold front associated with the upper trough finally swings through 
the area Sunday morning to afternoon, bringing an end to any 
lingering showers. This front won't bring much of an airmass change 
as temps still reach the 80s and humidity lingers.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Dry conditions expected early next week ahead 
of a midweek cold front. 

Upper-level ridging begins to build over the Southeast beginning 
Monday and into Tuesday as the cold front transitions offshore. 
Humidity & temperatures decrease in the wake of the cold front on 
Monday, with dewpoints ranging in the 50s and low 60s as mid-level 
dry air transitions overhead. Monday night might be the first 
fall night of widespread lows in the 50s.

Overall, anticipate seasonal, dry conditions to persist over the 
following days as this ridging continues to build into the midweek 
period. Beginning Wednesday, this ridging begins to transition into 
more of a zonal flow overhead as a trough further north forms over 
Quebec and Nova Scotia. An associated cold front could begin to 
track across the East Coast sometime during this period, although 
current guidance shows some spread in the timing of this frontal 
passage. This front could bring some showers and thunderstorms to 
the region, but probability of severe weather remains low at this 
time. 

&&

.AVIATION /18Z FRIDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
A few thunderstorms are possible around CHO through late this 
afternoon. A front that is moving south of the area today is going 
to stall tonight, then lift north as a warm front Saturday. Expect 
sub-VFR conditions to overspread the area from south to north 
Saturday morning. There is uncertainty as to how far north the sub-
VFR CIGs are, but likely impact most of the terminals. Widespread 
showers and scattered thunderstorms are expected areawide Saturday 
afternoon into late Saturday evening. TEMPO groups are likely to be 
needed, but are just beyond the current TAF period. 

A couple of reinforcing cold fronts move through the region Sunday 
into Sunday night, with VFR conditions returning in WNW/NW winds.

Prevailing VFR conditions are anticipated across terminals Monday 
through Wednesday. A few lingering showers could temporarily bring 
reduced conditions near KCHO on Monday, but otherwise conditions 
remain mostly clear throughout Tuesday & Wednesday. Northerly winds 
shift southeasterly by Tuesday night. 

&&

.MARINE...
A slow moving front continues to slide south through the waters. The 
brief surge of winds earlier this morning has now abated, with 
overall north winds around 10 knots. The front stalls south of the 
waters tonight, then lifts north as a warm front Saturday night. An 
increase in winds over the waters Saturday could be near SCA levels. 
Late afternoon to late evening thunderstorms could lead to hazardous 
marine conditions, with Special Marine Warnings possibly needed. A 
secondary front moves through Sunday, then a stronger cold front on 
Monday. Wind gusts could increase to near marginal SCA thresholds
on Monday before diminishing throughout the day Tuesday. Winds stay
below SCA criteria through Wednesday. Northeasterly winds shift
southeasterly in the wake of a cold front by Tuesday night. 

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Strengthening onshore flow Saturday will bring tide levels up across 
the area. Some locations could reach Action Stage by Saturday night 
to early Sunday high tides. A cold front moves through Sunday, and 
again Monday, which should bring an end to any coastal flooding 
potential.

&&

.LWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
DC...None.
MD...None.
VA...None.
WV...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...KRR/SRT
AVIATION...KRR/SRT
MARINE...KRR/SRT
